findings.why: The take-home line states an absolute the article's own body disproves: shop-bought butter tteok is explicitly described earlier as unverified for celiac readers because of shared equipment and shared milling facilities. A reader who skims to the conclusion gets the opposite of the careful message.
findings.fix: Change to 'made from a naturally gluten-free base' or 'safe when you make it yourself from flours you've checked' — reserve any unqualified 'safe' for the home-made version only.

findings.quote: in Yeonnam is a dedicated gluten-free bakery-and-cafe where you don't have to vet a single ingredient
findings.why: This instructs a celiac reader to stop verifying at a specific named venue. Even a genuinely dedicated facility can change suppliers or add a wheat-handling product, and the article gives no basis or date for the 'dedicated' status it is asking readers to trust.
findings.fix: State how and when the dedicated status was confirmed (visit date, operator confirmation), and soften to 'a dedicated gluten-free bakery — still worth confirming on the day, as with any venue'.

findings.quote: As of recently, **E-Mart's No Brand line and various online grocery malls sell a pre-mixed blend of glutinous rice flour and tapioca starch.**
findings.why: A specific retailer and product line are named with no product name, no link, and no purchase date, so no reader can confirm the product exists or is still stocked. 'Various online grocery malls' compounds the uncheckability. This is exactly where hallucinated retail detail hides.
findings.fix: Name the exact product as printed on the bag, state where and when it was bought, and link the listing — or drop the brand and say only that pre-mixed blends have started appearing.

findings.quote: check the bag for a shared-facility (같은 제조시설) statement
findings.why: In Korea the shared-facility line is a voluntary advisory, not a mandated disclosure, and mandatory allergen labelling covers wheat only — not barley or rye. A reader who finds no such statement may wrongly conclude the flour was milled cleanly.
findings.fix: Add one sentence: Korea mandates wheat on allergen labels but not barley or rye, and the shared-facility line is voluntary — its absence is not evidence of a clean facility. Contact the manufacturer if it matters.

findings.quote: Around **6,000 won for three pieces, plus another 500 won to add condensed milk.**
findings.why: The price anchors the article's central argument that home-making is cheaper, but it has no shop, no city, and no date attached, so a reader cannot tell whether it still holds or ever applied to their neighbourhood.
findings.fix: Attach the vendor type, area, and month of purchase, e.g. 'a Seongsu cafe, July 2026' — and note that trend-dessert pricing moves fast.

findings.quote: Plain rice cake, and simple desserts like butter tteok, are naturally gluten-free.
